\[
\hat{F}(f) = \begin{cases} G(f) / H(f) & |f| \le D_0,\ |H(f)| \ge \epsilon \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases},\quad D_0 = 0.71,\ \epsilon = 0.05
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(G, H, F\): The spectra of the blurred image, the PSF and the estimate
- \(D_0\): The cutoff radius in cycles per pixel
- \(\epsilon\): The smallest gain that is divided

A blur multiplies the spectrum F of the image by H, the transform of the PSF h, so G = H F. Dividing by H gives F back. Where |H| is very small, the blur removed the frequency and any noise is divided by almost 0. The filter therefore divides only where |H| reaches the threshold and within the cutoff radius, as Gonzalez and Woods limit the inverse filter to a radius. H is the FFT of h placed with its center at the origin of the grid. The PSF is the kernel of the Gaussian filter cut at 4 sigma, of the motion blur filter, or of the disk averaging filter.
